newsitem.title: FRANCE: Judge sends French former minister to trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge sends French former minister to trial.

text.p: A French judge on Monday ordered former industry minister Gerard Longuet to stand trial over the financing of his Riviera holiday but dropped a more serious probe into misuse of corporate funds, justice sources said.

Investigating magistrate Mireille Filippini said Longuet, who quit the cabinet two years ago in a corruption probe, must stand trial on suspicion that he benefited from suspiciously generous credit terms.
The businessman who built the luxury villa, in the resort of Saint Tropez, was also ordered to stand trial in connection with the credit granted to Longuet.

Longuet hailed the decision to drop the probe into misuse of corporate funds as evidence that he was innocent, and announced that he would stand in a general election next year to relaunch his political career.
"It is clear that an ordinary citizen would have been spared prosecution...This ordeal was inflicted on me only because I was a cabinet minister," he said in a statement.
Longuet faces yet another probe in connection with the funding of his centrist Republican Party, however.

Currently the president of the Lorraine regional council in eastern France, Longuet was one of three ministers who resigned from the cabinet of ex-prime minister Edouard Balladur on suspicion of corruption in the run-up to 1995 presidential elections.
Balladur stood in the election and lost to fellow-Gaullist Jacques Chirac.
